summary:
EIGHT findings re-verified against the current tree BEFORE any edit: all eight reproduce, none was already fixed, none is wrong. FIVE FIXED (the two MEDIUMs, and three of the LOWs); THREE NOT FIXED BECAUSE THE FILE IS NOT MINE OR THE RULING IS DEFERRED, each named with how I established it. All edits are confined to src/capacity/api.py plus one corrected sentence in .rework/audits/close_capacity_eval.json; src/eval/** needed no code change and got none.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, in one line: cap.valve printed FIRED on six of the eight corners of the standard sweep for a valve that cannot lift on any of them, and cap.vocab_arm_honest printed UNREACHABLE on two corners where the arm is armed and lifting. Those are the two halves of the same collapse D15 was written to refuse, one on each side of it, in the two lines either side of the fix D15 recorded.

THE MEASUREMENT, all three revisions rebuilt rather than reasoned about. cap.vocab_arm_honest.reachable across CAP_TARGETS x LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS: git 8cb00e3 (pre-D15) 5 of 8; HEAD (D15 as shipped) 2 of 8; repaired tree 4 of 8, and they are exactly targets in (vocab, both) -- which is the criterion close_capacity_eval.json::recommendation.measurement stated and the tree did not meet. cap.valve: FIRED on 6 of 8 before, UNREACHABLE on 8 of 8 after, because the SHIPPED default resolves both soft caps to the hard ceiling and a cap at its ceiling has no room to earn. The neighbouring controls still fire: CAP_TARGETS=experts CAP_FAB_START=1000 -> FIRED; =1844 (the settling point exactly) -> FIRED; =1845 -> UNREACHABLE naming the settling point; CAP_TARGETS=vocab CAP_VOCAB_START=2048 -> FIRED on both gates.

NO WIRE WAS SPENT. cap.valve's new arithmetic reads d_operating_population, which was ALREADY declared for CAP in spine/assemble.py::COUPLINGS, already delivered onto CAP's frozen Config, and already listed in CAP's package-level 'Wires read' line in docs/04_CONTRACT.md. The ledger is untouched at 23 of 25; test_ownership O4 and test_contract K5 both still pass, now counting one more read site for that wire.

SUITE GREEN before and after. Three files in the tree are modified by OTHER agents and not by me -- src/data/api.py, src/opt/api.py + src/opt/levers.py, src/sig/api.py + src/sig/levers.py -- established two ways: all are outside the src/capacity and src/eval I own and I never wrote to those paths, and their untracked report files (.rework/audits/close_data_counters.json, repair_sig.json, v_opt_*.json) sit beside mine from this same run.

recommendation.chose:
cap.valve's REACHABILITY is keyed on whether a lift can actually go anywhere, arm by arm, and not on the package switch: an armed arm is dead on arrival if its soft cap is <= 0 (the growth clamp goes negative on the first flush -- C30), if the cap is >= its hard ceiling (no room to earn: derive.lift_to returns cap + max(floor, frac*cap), which from a cap at the ceiling lands above it and is refused as at_hard_ceiling), or -- expert arm only -- if the cap is above d_operating_population (the population never reaches it, so it never pins). UNREACHABLE when no armed arm can lift, with the arithmetic printed and every dead arm named with its lever and its value; FIRED when one can, with any OTHER dead arm still named in the reason so a half-dead valve is not reported as simply live.

cap.vocab_arm_honest's mask-off branch becomes the MIDDLE state (fired=False, reachable=True, reason printed) instead of UNREACHABLE, because the arm is armed, the lift happens, and nothing refuses it.

FIRED ON cap.valve IS DECLARED TO BE THE ARMING ANSWER, IN THE PRINTED LINE ITSELF. The gate is built at startup, before the first flush, so no lift can have happened; the reason on the fired arm says exactly that and points at CAP.counters' lifts_experts / lifts_vocab as where the lifts are counted. That converts the verifier's second half of MEDIUM #2 -- 'FIRED means the switch is on, not a lift happened' -- from a silent misuse into a stated convention that the reader of the report sees without opening the file.
recommendation.alternatives:
ON THE MEANING OF `fired` FOR cap.valve, which is the only real choice here.
(A) What I did: fired = 'armed AND able to lift', stated in the printed reason. COST: the word FIRED still does not mean 'a lift happened'.
(B) fired=False + reason on the armed arm, so the line reads 'armed, did not fire (0 lifts)' and the gate uses all three states. COST, and it is why I did not: nothing rebuilds this Gate -- observe and counters are both stubs -- so a valve that DID lift would print 'armed, did not fire' for the whole run, which is a false statement rather than an imprecise one. It also puts a lift count on a startup line whose declared home is CAP.counters, i.e. a second source of truth for the number this package exists to report.
(C) Rename the gate to cap.valve_armed so the name carries the meaning. COST: it breaks the name .rework/DECISIONS.md D15 uses to describe this exact gate, and the audit that produced D15 already rejected renaming a declared report surface as out of proportion (its alternative D). A reader arriving from D15 would grep for a name that no longer exists.
(D) Split cap.valve into cap.expert_arm / cap.vocab_arm. COST: two new declared gate names, and it does not fix anything the per-arm reasons in (A) do not already say.

ON THE MASK-OFF BRANCH.
(E) What I did: middle state. COST: one more configuration on which the line is not UNREACHABLE, which a reader skimming for 'what was inert' must now read the reason of -- exactly what spine/gate.py::Gate.line prints reasons on every arm for.
(F) Keep UNREACHABLE and ADD the refusal, so the sentence 'declared dishonest rather than lifted silently' becomes true. COST: it needs a new entry in Decision.block_reason's closed set or a third startup_refusals clause, and that closed set is written into docs/04_CONTRACT.md's CAP section, which I do not own -- so it is a two-file change with a doc I may not edit, and K1 compares the document and the tree in both directions. Referred below rather than taken.
(G) Leave it. COST: the package keeps reporting an arm as inert while it lifts, which is the reading the whole gate record exists to refuse.
recommendation.evidence:
THE EIGHT CORNERS, cap.valve, before -> after. off/{0,1}: UNREACHABLE (off vs off) -> unchanged. experts/{0,1}, vocab/{0,1}, both/{0,1}: 'FIRED (<targets> vs off)' -> 'UNREACHABLE (experts 4096/ceiling 4096/settles 1844 vs a soft cap in 1..ceiling-1 that the population can reach) -- CAP_TARGETS=experts arms the valve and no armed arm can lift: the expert arm's soft cap is 4096 against a hard ceiling of 4096 (CAP_FAB_START=0, sentinel 0 -> hard ceiling 4096), so there is no room to earn ...'. That is six FIRED readings for a dead mechanism, removed.

THE CONTROLS, which is the half that proves I did not simply make the gate always unreachable. CAP_TARGETS=experts CAP_FAB_START=1000 -> 'FIRED (experts 1000/ceiling 4096/settles 1844 ...)'. CAP_FAB_START=1844 -> FIRED; CAP_FAB_START=1845 -> UNREACHABLE naming the settling point, so the boundary is exactly the one startup_refusals declares ('at or below the settling point'). CAP_TARGETS=vocab CAP_VOCAB_START=2048 -> FIRED. CAP_TARGETS=both CAP_FAB_START=3000 CAP_VOCAB_START=2048 -> FIRED, with '... ONE ARMED ARM IS STILL DEAD ON ARRIVAL: the expert arm's soft cap is 3000 against a cull settling point of 1844 ...' appended, so the live arm does not hide the dead one.

THE VOCABULARY GATE. vocab/0 and both/0 go from 'UNREACHABLE (False vs True) -- LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0: the vocabulary arm can lift, but ...' to 'armed, did not fire (False vs True) -- LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0: the vocabulary arm IS armed, so this precondition was TESTED AND NOT MET ... NOTHING REFUSES THE LIFT -- observe's block-reason set has no entry for unmasked dead rows and neither startup_refusals clause covers it -- so the run lifts anyway and this line is the only place that says the lift was dishonest.' vocab/1 and both/1 are unchanged at 'FIRED (True vs True)' and off/* and experts/* are unchanged at UNREACHABLE, which is the control for D15.

THE CLOSED SET THE REASON CITES WAS READ, NOT ASSUMED: capacity/api.py::observe's DID IT FIRE line lists targets_off | not_pinned | warmup | blackout | not_stalled | threshold | at_hard_ceiling and has no honesty entry, and capacity/api.py::startup_refusals' two clauses are the population clamp and the settling-point coupling.
recommendation.measurement:
cap.vocab_arm_honest.reachable over the eight corners, on THREE revisions built from source rather than argued about: a scratch copy of src/ with capacity/api.py replaced by `git show 8cb00e3:` gives reachable=True on 5 (off/0, off/1, experts/1, vocab/1, both/1); the same with `git show HEAD:` gives 2 (vocab/1, both/1); the repaired working tree gives 4 (vocab/0, vocab/1, both/0, both/1). So close_capacity_eval.json's 'Before: reachable on 6 of 8 ... After: reachable on exactly 4 of 8' was wrong in both directions -- 5 and 2 -- and its stated criterion ('True on exactly the four where a vocabulary lift is possible, i.e. targets in (vocab, both)') is met by the tree for the first time today. That field is corrected in place, with both old numbers quoted.

cap.valve: fired on 6 of 8 before (every corner but `off`), on 0 of 8 after -- correct, because the sweep never sets a start lever and the sentinel resolves both caps to the hard ceiling. Reachability returns the moment a start lever gives the valve somewhere to go, which the six control builds above show.

Scripts, outside the repository, under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad: vcap/one_corner.py and vcap/sentinel.py (the verifier's, reused unchanged), rcap/count.py (the three-revision reachability count), rcap/pre and rcap/shipped (the two scratch source trees).

changed.title: MEDIUM (finding 2, DEFECT_CONFIRMED, FIXED): cap.valve printed FIRED on six of eight corners for a valve that cannot lift -- the collapse D15 fixed for the vocabulary arm, printed by the sibling gate one line up for the expert arm
changed.what_changed: src/capacity/api.py::new_valve. The gate was `Gate('cap.valve', targets != 'off', targets, 'off')` with an UNREACHABLE arm only at targets == 'off', so its `fired` value and its reachability were the same predicate and every armed corner printed FIRED. It now computes, per arm, whether a lift can go anywhere: expert_room = armed and 0 < cap_experts < hard_experts and cap_experts <= d_operating_population; vocab_room = armed and 0 < cap_vocab < hard_vocab. UNREACHABLE when no armed arm qualifies, with each dead arm's lever, value, ceiling and (for experts) settling point in the reason; FIRED when one does, with any other dead arm still named. The fired arm's reason states that FIRED here is the ARMING answer and not a lift, and points at CAP.counters for the lift counts. new_valve's WIRES READ line now names d_operating_population with the reason it is read here as well as in startup_refusals, and the DID IT FIRE line's claim that BOTH gates carry all three of gate.py's states is corrected: cap.valve carries two, because at startup 'can a lift happen at all' has no middle state.
changed.proof: BEFORE: `python3 <scratch>/vcap/one_corner.py experts 0` printed 'Gate cap.valve: FIRED (experts vs off)' with wires d_expert_slots=4096 d_operating_population=1844 on the same build, and the same at experts/1, vocab/{0,1}, both/{0,1}. AFTER, the same command prints 'Gate cap.valve: UNREACHABLE (experts 4096/ceiling 4096/settles 1844 vs a soft cap in 1..ceiling-1 that the population can reach) -- ... the expert arm's soft cap is 4096 against a hard ceiling of 4096 (CAP_FAB_START=0, sentinel 0 -> hard ceiling 4096), so there is no room to earn: every lift derive.lift_to computes lands above the ceiling and is refused as at_hard_ceiling'. NEIGHBOURING CASES, still reachable: CAP_FAB_START=1000 -> FIRED; =1844 -> FIRED; =1845 -> UNREACHABLE naming the settling point; CAP_TARGETS=vocab CAP_VOCAB_START=2048 -> FIRED; CAP_TARGETS=both CAP_FAB_START=3000 CAP_VOCAB_START=2048 -> FIRED with the dead expert arm named. 'The sentinel, the operator, and the checkpoint, in that order of precedence.' named the sentinel FIRST though it resolves LAST, and did not name `targets == "off"` at all though that is the first branch and beats every other. Replaced by the four branches in the order the body decides them, with the old sentence quoted and the reason it is a live contradiction rather than a wording preference recorded: every OTHER statement of the precedence in this file -- new_valve's docstring, the two inline comments, the four origin strings -- was already right, so the one-line summary a reader skims was the only wrong one.
changed.proof: The body's four returns, in source order, are: `if targets == "off": return hard, 'off (valve disabled; ...)'`; `if given:` -> the operator (with an explicit 0 routed to the hard ceiling); `if restored is not None and restored.get(what) is not None:` -> the checkpoint; then the bare `return hard, f'sentinel 0 -> hard ceiling {hard}'`. Confirmed live: CAP_TARGETS=both CAP_FAB_START=256 -> origin 'operator (fab_start=256)'; CAP_TARGETS=off CAP_FAB_START=256 -> origin 'off (valve disabled; the cap is the hard ceiling)', i.e. `off` beating an explicit operator value, which the old sentence did not admit was possible.

changed.what_changed:
TWO EDITS, and the split is the point. (1) src/capacity/api.py::new_valve: both shapes are now VISIBLE. cap.valve's new arithmetic treats cap <= 0 and cap >= ceiling as dead-on-arrival, so CAP_TARGETS=experts CAP_FAB_START=-5 prints 'UNREACHABLE ... the expert arm's soft cap is -5 (CAP_FAB_START=-5, operator (fab_start=-5)), and a cap at or below zero makes the growth clamp negative on the first flush, freezing fabric growth for the whole run (C30)' and =99999 prints the no-room-to-earn arm against the 4096 ceiling. (2) src/capacity/api.py::startup_refusals clause (1) now spells out that a cap at or below zero IS this clause -- it is below any population there can be -- naming the two levers and saying that the 2026-09-03 sentinel repair left this shape open when it moved an explicit 0 out of the soft-cap space.
WHAT I DID NOT DO, deliberately: I did not make new_valve RAISE on a negative cap. This tree's refusals are strings returned from startup_refusals and collected by the composition root, not exceptions from a builder; K2 says the root raises nothing but NotImplementedError and that it comes from a stub. Inventing a second refusal channel in a live body to close a P4 schedule gap would be a bigger change than the defect, and it would put CAP's refusals in two places.

AFTER: the resolved value is unchanged (-5 is still what the operator asked for and the origin still records it), but at CAP_TARGETS=experts the gate reads 'UNREACHABLE (experts -5/ceiling 4096/settles 1844 ...)' with the C30 sentence, and at CAP_TARGETS=both it reads FIRED on the live vocabulary arm with ' ONE ARMED ARM IS STILL DEAD ON ARRIVAL: the expert arm's soft cap is -5 ...' appended -- so the dead arm is named even when the valve as a whole is alive. `python3 -c "from spine import compose; compose.compose(environ={})"` still halts at 'CAP.startup_refusals: P4 (capacity) fills this in', unchanged, which is the honest statement that the REFUSAL is still owed.
